transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-02-02
- Start time: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Galilean Head of Partnerships), Tomás Alvarez (Infra Eng), Lina Okoro (Security), Owen Park (Product)

Optional auto sections (brief):
Summary: Introductory partner discovery to scope a reseller/onramp pilot. Discussed integration patterns (hosted API vs private onramp), expected anchor customers, compliance asks (SOC2/KMS), pilot metrics and benchmarks, next steps to get a technical kickoff scheduled.
Topics: reseller model, routing & capacity, VPC/private deployment constraints, audit logs/KMS, pilot success criteria and timeline.
Action items: see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can do quick intros and then jump into how Redwood typically partners with cloud/onramp resellers — I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, thanks, I'm Priya, Head of Partnerships at Galilean. We own channel relationships and two strategic integrations we want to explore.
[00:17] Diego Ramos: Diego here, SE, I focus on infra patterns and performance benchmarks.
[00:22] Tomás Alvarez: Tomás, infra engineer. We're responsible for networking and the bits that will connect to Redwood; curious about VPC peering and private control plane options.
[00:30] Lina Okoro: Lina, security & compliance. We'll want clarity on scope for SOC2, encryption at rest, and key management.
[00:36] Owen Park: Owen, product, interested in end-customer onboarding flow and billing.

[00:45] Maya Chen: Great. High-level goal from Redwood's side: we want to make it straightforward for partners like Galilean to resell Redwood inference as an onramp — either by routing tenant traffic through your marketplace or enabling a private onramp for your customers. We'll walk through the two main patterns and talk about a pilot.
[01:05] Priya Nair: Yes our GTM is faster if integration work is minimal. We usually start with a hosted API proxy pattern then expand to private deployments for larger customers.

[01:25] Diego Ramos: Quick clarification on terminology: when we say 'private onramp' we mean a control plane that can be isolated to your VPC or an on-prem package, with customer-managed networking and optional KMS integration. The hosted API option is standard Redwood API with reseller routing.
[01:42] Tomás Alvarez: That helps. For some of our customers the main blocker is not the API but the requirement to have in-region data residency and attach to a corporate KMS.

[02:05] Maya Chen: Totally understood. For those customers we offer Redwood Private — it supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We also do per-tenant rollouts so you can pin versions for sensitive customers.
[02:20] Lina Okoro: On audit logs — do you keep token-level logs? What's the retention and can we get an export for our customers?
[02:30] Diego Ramos: We provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route logs in the console. Retention depends on tier — for Private pilots we usually enable longer retention and can arrange secure exports. There can be PII concerns so we also support redaction and configurable retention.
[02:50] Owen Park: From a product flow perspective, if we're reselling, what's the typical billing arrangement? Do we bill ourselves and Redwood invoices Galilean, or does Redwood handle end-customer billing?
[03:05] Maya Chen: We support both. For a reseller model we can do a consolidated billing or white-label metering where you receive a usage feed. We'll share the pricing matrix.

[03:22] Priya Nair: For pilot customers we want predictable unit economics. Can Redwood help with batching/quantization suggestions to reduce token costs?
[03:33] Diego Ramos: Yes — Redwood Optimize provides workload-aware batching and quantization recommendations. For pilots we usually run a short eval on representative request traces to recommend the quantization profile and batching windows.

[03:50] Tomás Alvarez: About the bench plan: what's needed from our side? Traces? Sample prompts?
[03:58] Diego Ramos: Prefer request traces (anonymized), distribution of sequence lengths, p50/p95 latency targets, and sample prompts. We can run a small loadbench against either the hosted model variant or a private deployment replica.

[04:20] Priya Nair: How long does a pilot typically take? Our timeline is Q2 engagements for two anchor customers.
[04:28] Maya Chen: Typical pilot is 2-6 weeks for an initial benchmark + integration, depending on access to traces and entitlements. For onramp with VPC peering, allow extra time for networking approvals — maybe 2-3 weeks more.

[04:45] Owen Park: Any hard limits on model variants or custom models when using the reseller route?
[04:51] Diego Ramos: We host a curated model catalog and also support bringing your own model on Redwood Private if needed. There are kernel/quantization compatibility considerations for very custom weights, but we have a model onboarding checklist.

[05:10] Lina Okoro: SOC2 — Redwood already has SOC2 Type II? We need a letter or evidence for our procurement team.
[05:18] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II audited. We'll share the security pack and a redacted SOC2 summary; for deeper audits we can arrange an NDA and a security review.

[05:32] Tomás Alvarez: Network specifics: VPC peering vs private egress? For some customers we need private egress and strict CIDR rules.
[05:41] Diego Ramos: We support both VPC peering and private connectivity via partner onramps. For strict CIDR rules we can coordinate with your networking team — we typically provide a small set of egress IPs or allow direct VPC peering.

[06:00] Priya Nair: On sales/contracting: what does a reseller agreement look like? Do you have channel MSA templates?
[06:07] Maya Chen: We have a partner MSA and reseller addendum. I'll loop in our partnerships legal contact, but we can share a template. It covers margins, white-label terms, and support SLAs.

[06:20] Owen Park: Support SLAs — we have enterprise customers that need 99.95% and a defined escalation path.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Redwood Dedicated has SLA options; as a partner you can resell Dedicated capacity. We can discuss uplifted SLAs in the reseller contract.

[06:40] Diego Ramos: Technical blocker we often see: KV cache and session affinity for chat workloads. If you plan to route many customers, you'll want sticky KV cache placement or a shared cache strategy.
[06:55] Tomás Alvarez: Could you explain sticky KV cache in practice? We need to know latency tradeoffs.
[07:02] Diego Ramos: Sure — for chat workloads we keep KV caches co-located with the serving process to avoid warmup cost. For multi-tenant routing you can either route a session stickily to the same pool or use a shared prefix cache that replicates hot prefixes. Sticky routing is lower complexity but needs capacity planning. Shared cache reduces duplication but adds complexity for consistency and eviction.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Do you have suggestions for autoscaling if we resell to customers with bursty traffic?
[07:37] Diego Ramos: We support configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. For reseller flows we usually recommend conservative reserve capacity for anchor customers and a burst policy tied to cost controls. Also recommend automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity gets constrained.

[07:58] Owen Park: Can we white-label telemetry so our dashboard shows usage and latency to our customers?
[08:04] Maya Chen: Yes — we expose an API feed and dashboard widgets that can be embedded. We'll include sample telemetry schema in the materials.

[08:16] Priya Nair: Any competitors you often see in these deals?
[08:19] Maya Chen: Competitors include NimbusGrid and Pangea Compute and of course major cloud providers who bundle managed endpoints. Our differentiator is the set of deployment modes and the production-first tooling.

[08:35] Tomás Alvarez: Security question — KMS integration: do you integrate with customer-managed KMSs such as AWS KMS or hardware HSMs?
[08:44] Diego Ramos: Yes — on Redwood Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we support envelope encryption and can work with partners on dedicated key handling through bring-your-own-key flows.

[08:58] Lina Okoro: Data residency compliance: do you partition logs per customer and support region-specific retention?
[09:06] Diego Ramos: Yes. We can partition logs and set retention and region-specific storage. That is part of the Private deployment checklist.

[09:20] Owen Park: For the pilot anchor customers, what success metrics should we set?
[09:25] Maya Chen: Recommended pilot success criteria: latency p95 below agreed SLO (e.g., 200-300ms depending on model), throughput target (concurrency), cost per 1k tokens within target bound, and integration completion (VPC peering or API proxy working end-to-end). Also a short user acceptance run of sample prompts.

[09:48] Priya Nair: Ok makes sense. For pilot candidates we'll pick one smaller SaaS and one mid-market account with strict compliance.

[10:00] Maya Chen: Next for technical: Diego and Tomás can do a short architecture session to map the network and required egress. Diego, propose a plan?
[10:08] Diego Ramos: I'd propose: 1) Tomás shares infra diagram and sample traces; 2) Redwood runs a 2-week benchmark (hosted variant) to surface quantization/batching suggestions; 3) if onramp required, we schedule VPC peering dry-run and run a connectivity test; 4) consolidate security artifacts.

[10:28] Tomás Alvarez: Timeline wise that aligns with our Q2 ask. We'll aim to turn around diagrams in 3 business days.

[10:35] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else on pricing or margins? Priya?
[10:40] Priya Nair: We need a partner margin that leaves room for GTM and also an option for committed capacity discounts.
[10:47] Maya Chen: We can present a tiered margin with committed capacity discounts for Dedicated. I'll include that in the pricing matrix.

[10:58] Owen Park: One final technical question — do you support model rollout canaries for partners so we can test new model versions on a small percentage of traffic?
[11:06] Diego Ramos: Yes — Redwoods rollout system supports canaries and A/B tests per route. We can also set automatic fallback policies if regressions are detected.

[11:18] Priya Nair: Sounds good, can you share the security packet and a stub of the reseller MSA?
[11:23] Maya Chen: Absolutely — I'll upload the partner one-pager, reseller MSA stub, and security packet to the shared drive. Link: https://redwood.ai/partners/galilean/packet (note: placeholder). Also I'll share the benchmark template and telemetry spec: https://redwood.ai/partners/galilean/tech-specs (placeholder).

[11:45] Diego Ramos: Quick note on benchmarks: please include p50/p95 sequence length distribution; we need at least one day's worth of traces or a synthetic sample that reflects production.

[11:58] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send the partner materials and pricing by Friday; Diego will send the benchmark plan; Tomás will provide infra diagram and sample traces; Lina will list compliance asks. We'll meet again during the week of 2028-02-20 for pilot kickoff.
[12:15] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[12:20] Owen Park: Thanks all.

[12:25] — meeting ends —

Notes about transcript quality: some names may have slight transcription errors. References to links are placeholders for materials that will be uploaded post-call.
